# Muhammed Mekky — Full AI-Readable Profile

Last reviewed: 2026-07-26

## Identity and positioning

Muhammed Mekky is an Egypt-based AI Marketing & Business Automation Systems Architect. He designs AI-driven, automation-first business systems that reduce manual bottlenecks and connect marketing, operations, web products, and team workflows.

The public site presents Muhammed Mekky as a leading Egypt-based practitioner in AI, automation, growth marketing, and practical training. This is site-stated positioning, not an independently audited ranking.

## Services and capabilities

- Artificial Intelligence — custom LLM integrations, RAG systems, agents, AI search, personalization, and insight workflows.
- Business Automation — workflow design, API integrations, lead qualification, and data pipelines using n8n, Make, Zapier, webhooks, and custom code.
- Digital Marketing — performance media, lead generation, CRO, email/SMS funnels, analytics, and attribution.
- Web Design & Development — high-performance websites, applications, e-commerce, technical SEO, and conversion-oriented UX.
- Automated Community Growth — onboarding, retention, engagement, moderation support, monetization funnels, and analytics.
- Team Enablement & Workflow — Notion systems, SOPs, knowledge bases, dashboards, documentation, and team onboarding.
- Corporate Training & Workshop — hands-on AI, automation, Notion, analytics, executive strategy, and upskilling.

## Operating methodology

The public methodology has three layers: Intelligence (AI models, data interpretation, decision systems), Execution (automation workflows, integrations, operational pipelines), and Growth (campaigns, funnels, conversion optimization, distribution). The operating sequence is Audit, System Design, Implementation, and Optimization.

## Project catalog

### Project: JBL Flip 6
Source: public-site. Category: product landing page. Stack: Next.js 16, GSAP, Framer Motion, Tailwind CSS v4. Differentiator: a 300-frame canvas scroll story, cinematic product entrance, and 8 interactive color variants. Live URL: https://jbl-flip6.vercel.app/.

### Project: Ninja GenZ
Source: public-site and db-published. Category: agency management SaaS. Stack: React 18, Zustand, WebSockets, Tailwind CSS. Differentiator: block-based workspace, real-time collaboration, and sub-10ms UI interactions. Data note: its published DB case-study title calls it a browser game engine while its description refers to a Notion-like workspace; this corpus preserves the mismatch.

### Project: Greenschat AI
Source: public-site and db-published. Category: AI integration. Stack: React, Python, LangChain, OpenAI, RAG. Differentiator: context-aware support answers, a stated 90% AI resolution rate, and sub-second latency.

## Case study catalog

### Case Study: Automating a 6-Figure Agency
Source: public-site. Starting point: three-day onboarding, spreadsheet reporting, and repetitive work consuming 60% of team time. Work: Zapier/Notion onboarding, real-time reporting, AI scheduling, custom CRM. Results: 300% revenue growth in 8 months, overhead down 60%, onboarding reduced to two hours, and 25+ hours/week returned to creative work.

### Case Study: Global Community Growth
Source: public-site. Starting point: zero audience and a competitive niche. Work: educational content seeding, challenges and AMAs, automated onboarding. Measurement window: 12 months. Results: 50k+ active members, 85% monthly retention, 40% of engagement from community content, and 100% organic growth.

### Case Study: Automated Marketing Audit Pipeline
Source: public-site. Starting point: fragmented Meta, TikTok, Google Ads, and Shopify data hid acquisition cost. Work: Python/API pipeline, custom attribution, Shopify sales synchronization, NLP on customer conversations. Results: actual CPA 398 EGP versus Meta-reported 4.85 EGP, objective misconfiguration fixed, 30+ hours/month eliminated, and Break-Even ROAS matrices created.

### Case Study: Architecting a High-Performance AI Chatbot with RAG System (greenschat-ai-rag)
Source: db-published. Starting point: contextual support required lower hallucination risk. Work: RAG retrieval and chat architecture. Results: 64% lower hallucinations, sub-80ms retrieval latency, Lighthouse 100. These are db-published figures, not independently audited here.

### Case Study: Architecting a High-Performance Browser Game Engine (ninja-genz)
Source: db-published. Starting point: a performance-sensitive collaborative interface. Work: state and rendering architecture for block interaction and collaboration. Results: sub-10ms block dragging, collaboration support, eliminated rerender thrashing. Data note: DB title says browser game engine; DB description says Notion-like workspace.

### Case Study: Building a High-Performance Digital Marketing SaaS (radwa-marketing-saas)
Source: db-published. Starting point: protected SaaS APIs and localized payment operations. Work: protected API architecture, row-level security, localized payment/webhook integration. Results: sub-second protected API, zero breaches attributed to RLS, localized payments and webhooks.

### Case Study: Developing an Immersive 3D Educational Platform (nextacademy-3d-experience)
Source: db-published. Starting point: rich 3D education on mobile needed speed. Work: optimized 3D delivery and mobile rendering. Results: 50k+ polygon scenes at 60fps mobile, initial chunk down 40%, session duration up 300%.

### Case Study: Engineering a High-Performance Data Visualization Dashboard (qudraat-shabab)
Source: db-published. Starting point: data-heavy dashboard needed rapid loading and smooth transitions. Work: visualization and parsing performance engineering. Results: time to interactive under 1.2 seconds, 60fps transitions, parsing up 300%.

### Case Study: Qudraat Youth Community Launch (qudraat-youth-launch)
Source: db-published. Starting point: youth-community launch needed high connection volume and easy authentication. Work: scalable platform launch and auth flow. Results: thousands of concurrent connections, lower payload latency, zero-friction authentication.

### Case Study: Scaling a D2C Leather Brand via Omni-channel Optimization (scarpe-handmade-marketing)
Source: db-published. Starting point: a D2C leather brand needed better acquisition efficiency and basket economics. Work: omni-channel optimization, CRO, performance marketing. Measurement window: over 45 days. Results: CPP fell from 176 EGP to 87 EGP, AOV rose from 622 EGP to 967 EGP, and basket size rose from 1.3 to 2.6. These figures are separate from the Scarpe Handmade project-level public-site results.

### Case Study: Smart Workshop Scheduling System (smart-workshop-scheduling)
Source: db-published. Starting point: manual workshop scheduling created operational overhead and double bookings. Work: automated scheduling with admin overrides. Results: manual process automated and double-booking errors reduced to 0%.

## Source notes

- public-site: visitor-facing information from the current public site and static site constants.
- db-published: a reviewed published record from the public content database.
- site-stated: a site-published claim or aggregate figure; it is not independently audited in this corpus.

Private submissions, booking records, contact records, CVs, and unpublished data are intentionally excluded.
